title: Creating a non-native bio-amidation activity in asparagine synthetase via biosensor-guided directed evolution for the synthesis of (S)-2-aminobutyramide.
authors: Lai, Qianpeng; Meng, Yiwei; Liu, Zhongmei; Han, Laichuang; Guo, Junling; Peplowski, Lukasz; Cheng, Zhongyi; Zhou, Zhemin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物传感器定向进化改造天冬酰胺合成酶实现非天然酰胺化，虽用MD模拟分析底物结合模式，但核心是酶催化小分子底物转化，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与TF-DNA课题无关。
abstract: The direct asymmetric synthesis of chiral amides remains a focal point in green manufacturing, particularly for (S)-2-aminobutyramide whose traditional production is often hampered by low atom economy and arduous chiral resolution steps. Here, we report the creation of a non-native bio-amidation activity in Escherichia coli asparagine synthetase A (AsnA) for the proof-of-concept one-step biosynthesis of (S)-2-aminobutyramide, a critical intermediate for anti-epileptic drugs. To overcome the bottleneck of high-throughput screening, we engineered the AmiC-AmiR transcription factor into a highly sensitive biosensor (RC-4-Y83H) by remodeling its ligand-binding pocket, achieving a 23-fold induction response specifically toward (S)-2-AB. Utilizing this biosensor to screen saturation mutagenesis libraries, we identified an evolved variant (K77L/E120L/R255W) that showed a reversed substrate preference between the two substrates tested, converting (S)-2-aminobutyric acid to (S)-2-AB with retention of configuration. Molecular dynamics simulations and free-energy landscape analysis reveal that the mutations fundamentally remodel the active site, inducing a 180 degrees  flip of the substrate binding mode. This structural reorientation positions the non-native carboxyl group in a catalytically productive geometry relative to ATP, a conformation inaccessible in the wild-type enzyme. As a proof of concept, this work does not aim to deliver an industrially competitive biocatalyst; instead, it shows that the specificity of a native amide-forming enzyme can be reprogrammed toward a non-native alpha-amino acid, and it provides a generalizable, biosensor-guided framework for such reprogramming.
abstract_zh: 手性酰胺的直接不对称合成仍是绿色制造中的焦点，尤其是对于(S)-2-氨基丁酰胺，其传统生产常受限于低原子经济性和繁琐的手性拆分步骤。在此，我们报道在大肠杆菌天冬酰胺合成酶A（AsnA）中创建一种非天然生物酰胺化活性，用于概念验证的一步法生物合成(S)-2-氨基丁酰胺，这是抗癫痫药物的关键中间体。为克服高通量筛选的瓶颈，我们通过重塑AmiC-AmiR转录因子的配体结合口袋，将其工程化为高灵敏度生物传感器（RC-4-Y83H），实现了对(S)-2-AB的23倍诱导响应特异性。利用该生物传感器筛选饱和突变文库，我们鉴定出一个进化变体（K77L/E120L/R255W），其在所测试的两种底物之间表现出反转的底物偏好，将(S)-2-氨基丁酸转化为(S)-2-AB并保持构型。分子动力学模拟和自由能景观分析揭示，这些突变从根本上重塑了活性位点，诱导底物结合模式发生180度翻转。这种结构重定向使非天然羧基相对于ATP处于催化有利的几何构型，而这一构象在野生型酶中无法实现。作为概念验证，本研究并非旨在提供具有工业竞争力的生物催化剂；相反，它表明天然酰胺形成酶的特异性可被重编程以面向非天然α-氨基酸，并为此类重编程提供了一种可推广的、基于生物传感器的框架。
